items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.summary: Anthropic has granted an outside AI watchdog organization employee-like access to its operations, and the watchdog can publish its findings without needing Anthropic's approval first.
items.why_it_matters: It's a notable step toward independent, teeth-having oversight of a frontier AI lab rather than self-policing.

items.title: AI Trade Reversal Pierces Asia’s Star Picks-and-Shovels Stocks
items.summary: A deepening selloff in US technology stocks is spreading to Asia's AI supply-chain stocks, as mounting financing costs raise doubts about sustaining the AI infrastructure spending boom and threaten earnings across the region. CNBC and the Financial Times separately covered the broader market volatility and its uneven impact across chip stocks.
items.why_it_matters: It shows investor confidence in the AI buildout is wavering well beyond US markets.

items.title: Anthropic to Shift Some Shares Into New ‘Public Good’ Fund
items.summary: Anthropic PBC plans to shift 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund that can make donations addressing public-good issues, including mitigating AI's impact on the job market. TechCrunch separately reported the same share commitment.
items.why_it_matters: It signals how a major AI lab plans to address AI's societal and labor-market fallout as it keeps growing.

items.title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
items.summary: Anthropic's offensive research team published a report warning that self-replicating 'AI worms' are becoming a practical threat, since they need only modest capability on less powerful devices, and current trends suggest that capability will be feasible by the end of the year.
items.why_it_matters: It flags a concrete, near-term AI security risk rather than a speculative future scenario.

items.title: America’s $10tn AI infrastructure boom is starting to fray
items.summary: The Financial Times reports that the massive, roughly $10 trillion bet on AI infrastructure is starting to run into the unforgiving economics of building physical data centers and power supply at that scale.
items.why_it_matters: It's a reality check on whether the capital pouring into AI data centers can keep pace with physical and financial constraints.

items.title: DeepSeek Pushes Out Updated AI Model It Says Is Faster, Leaner
items.summary: DeepSeek released an updated AI model, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, over the weekend that the company says is faster and leaner, intensifying its challenge to Anthropic, OpenAI and domestic rivals like Moonshot Kimi and Z.ai. The model was also listed on Hugging Face and OpenRouter.
items.why_it_matters: It's another sign Chinese open-weight models are iterating fast and keeping pressure on Western labs' pricing and performance.

items.title: OpenAI Arrest Raises AI Espionage Concerns
items.summary: Bloomberg reports on the arrest of an OpenAI engineer accused of planting a covert recording device in an executive conference room, a case highlighting growing concern about protecting sensitive AI technology and trade secrets.
items.why_it_matters: It underscores how valuable frontier AI know-how has become a target for espionage.

items.title: Microsoft pulls out of AI datacentre project in Essex over power supply concerns
items.summary: Microsoft has withdrawn as anchor tenant from Nscale's planned AI datacentre in Loughton, Essex, which the UK government had hailed as the country's largest, citing concerns about power supply. Bloomberg separately confirmed Nscale said Microsoft withdrew from the deal, a setback for Nscale's IPO hopes.
items.why_it_matters: It shows power constraints, not just chip supply, are becoming a real bottleneck for AI datacentre buildouts.

items.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
items.summary: Meta's updated business terms had included language suggesting it could scrape and train AI on content from websites "associated" with its business users, including news publishers; after backlash, Meta removed that specific language, though a spokesperson said it didn't reflect any change in how Meta actually crawls the web. Legal experts quoted by Nieman Lab said the revised terms still grant broad scraping permissions.
items.why_it_matters: It's a live test of how much power platforms can claim over publishers' content for AI training.

items.title: Anthropic turns to lawyers to help AI agents strike deals
items.summary: The Financial Times reports that Anthropic is working with lawyers to establish rules of negotiation for cases where AI agents act and strike deals on humans' behalf.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights an overlooked legal gap as AI agents start taking real-world commercial actions for people.
